messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test `testNestedDOM` expects string values retrieved from an XML document to retain leading and trailing spaces, as indicated by the expected value `"foo;bar; baz "`. The current bug report indicates that JXPath automatically trims string values, removing such spaces (example: `<value> 12324 56</value>` becomes `'1234 56'` instead of `' 1234 56'`).

Examining the relevant code in `org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.dom.DOMNodePointer` shows the root cause:

- The method `stringValue(Node node)` is responsible for converting a DOM node to a string.
- For COMMENT_NODE, TEXT_NODE, CDATA_SECTION_NODE, and PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION_NODE types, the method retrieves the text but calls `.trim()` on the text before returning.
- For other node types with children, it recursively accumulates their text values but then trims the entire accumulated string before returning (`return buf.toString().trim();`).

Thus, the `.trim()` calls at multiple points in `stringValue` cause the automatic removal of leading and trailing whitespace on XML text nodes and other text-containing nodes. This behavior directly contradicts the test expectations and the issue report that leading or trailing spaces should be preserved exactly as in the original XML.

No relevant recent bug reports provide additional context, so the core issue is the unconditional trimming of string values in `DOMNodePointer.stringValue(Node)`.

Recommendations would involve modifying or removing these trimming operations to preserve whitespace as expected.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
